questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is common soil transmitted helminthic infection in India is Characterized by eggs in stool shown is the figure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Trichuris
  • Trichuris trichiura eggs are barrel-shaped, thick-shelled and possess a pair of polar “plugs” at each end.
  • The eggs are unembryonated when passed in stool

  • So according to this information the picture of egg in question showing brown colour, barrel shaped and bipolar mucus plug is indicative of Trichuris trichiura egg.

questions.stem: A 12 years old boy presents with vomiting within 3 hours of consumption of food at a party. What is the likely causative organism responsible for the symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Staphylococcus aureus
  • Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus (emetic type) have incubation period of less than 6hrs. rest all food poisoning microorganisms like Salmonella, clostridium have incubation period of more than 6 hrs so in this question boys developed food poisoning due to S. aureus.
  • Salmonella enteritidis - Most persons infected with Salmonellabacteria develop diarrhea, fever, and abdominal cramps 12 to 72 hours after infection

  • Staph aureus - Staph food poisoning is characterized by a sudden start of nausea, vomiting, and stomach cramps. Most people also have diarrhea.

  • Symptoms usually develop within 30 minutes to 8 hours after eating or drinking an item containing Staph toxin, and last no longer than 1 day. 

  • Clostridium Botulinum - In food-borne botulism, signs and symptoms include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea followed by constipation and abdominal distention. There may be weakness and difficulty breathing. Symptoms normally appear between 18 and 36 hours after consuming the contaminated food, but this can vary between 3 hours and 8 days

  • Clostridium perfringens - Symptoms of  perfringensfood poisoning include intense abdominal cramps and watery diarrhea. Your symptoms usually appear 6 to 24 hours after eating foods containing large numbers of C. perfringens. The disease usually is over within 24 hours. Less severe symptoms may last for 1 or 2 weeks

  •  Right answer in this context would be staphylococcus aureus food poisoning as symptoms develops within 3-4 hrs


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:162.

questions.stemHtml: A 5 years old boy presents with sore throat for the last two days. On examination he has a greyish white pseudo membrane around his tonsils. Diphtheria is suspected. What prophylactic step should be taken for the 3 years old younger sibling who has received immunization as per the schedule?

options.label: B
options.text: Prophylaxis with erythromycin and diphtheria antitoxin

options.label: D
options.text: Immunize with booster of diphtheria toxoid

questions.solutionHtml:
Nothing is required
  • As mentioned in the question, his sibling is fully immunized till date so according to the National immunization schedule his siblings have taken all the necessary doses of DPT so right now, nothing is required.
  • After 5-7yr of age his sibling may immunize with booster of diphtheria toxoid


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:158.

questions.stem: Recent influenza a pandemic was due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
H1N1
  • In the spring of 2009, a novel influenza A (H1N1) virus emerged. It was detected first in the United States and spread quickly across the United States and the world.
  • This new H1N1 virus contained a unique combination of influenza genes not previously identified in animals or people. This virus was designated as influenza A (H1N1) pdm09 virus.
  • H1N1 flu is also known as swine flu. It's called swine flu because in the past, the people who caught it had direct contact with pigs
  • H- Hemagglutinin N- Neuraminidase

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to be acquired by traumatic inoculation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sporothrix Schenckii
  • Sporotrichosis, caused by the dimorphic fungus Sporothrix schenckii, is currently distributed throughout the world, especially in tropical and subtropical zones.
  • Infection generally occurs by traumatic inoculation of soil, plants, and organic matter contaminated with the fungus. 
  • As all the mentioned organisms in the question are Dimorphic fungi
  • Except Sporothrix schenckii all three fungi acquired in body through inhalation



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number: 685.

questions.stemHtml: Shown in the figure is the HBV test. Which of the following is the principle of this test?
questions.solutionHtml:
Immunochromatography
  • HBsAg card test based on the principle of immunochromatography, a unique assay based on antigen capture or sandwich principle
  • The method uses monoclonal antibodies conjugated to colloidal gold and polyclonal antibodies immobilized on nitrocellulose strips in a thin line.
  • pribiciple of ict:
  • The immunochromatographic test principle is based on immunoaffinity partition of the analyte between sample migrating laterally through a porous membrane and a finite “affinity zone” prepared by immobilizing an antibody on the membrane.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:773.

questions.stem: Antiseptic property of bleaching powder is due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypochlorous acid

What is Bleaching Powder?

Calcium oxychloride (CaOCl2) is known as bleaching powder

Action

Bleaching powder or Calcium hypochlorite (CaOCl2) is mixed salt have two type of anion Cl-(chloride ion ) and OCl-(hypochlorite ion) .it act as oxidizing agent and bleaching agent

Bleaching powder has a lot of uses.

It is used for bleaching silk and wool.

It is mainly used as a bleaching agent for cotton, linen and wood pulp.

Bleaching action of bleaching powder is due to oxidation and it is permanent

CaOCl2 + H2O——-Ca(OH)2 + Cl2

Cl2 + H2O——- O +2HCl

COLOR+O—-> COLORLESS

  • Bleaching powder is used as disinfectant and germicide especially in the sterilization of drinking water.
  • It is used as an oxidizing agent in many chemical industries to obtain various chemical products.
  • C2H5OH+Cl2—->CH3CHO + 2HC

 Antiseptic property of breaching powder

Bleaching powder releases Hypochlorous acid that causes oxidative damage to the cells



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:669.

questions.stemHtml: An HIV positive patient with a CD4 count of 300/mm3 presents with mucosal lesion in the mouth. On microscopy budding yeasts and pseudo hyphae are seen. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Candidiasis
  • Candidiasis is a fungal infection due to any type of Candida. When it affects the mouth, it is commonly called thrush. Signs and symptoms include white patches on the tongue or other areas of the mouth and throat
  • Risk factors
  • Immunosuppression (HIV/AIDS), diabetes, corticosteroids


JAWETZ, EDITION 28TH: SECTION VII Diagnostic Medical Microbiology and Clinical Correlation, Page no: 815.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the cause of donovanosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Klebsiella granulomatis
  • Donovanosis is a sexually transmissible genital ulcer disease. The bacterium that causes donovanosis (Klebsiella granulomatis) infects the skin around the genitals, groin or anal area and causes ulcers and destruction of the skin.
  • Haemophilus ducreyi - It causes the sexually transmitted disease chancroid
  • Leishmania donovani- It causes leishmaniasis or kala azar
  • Treponema Pallidum- It causes syphilis, causing primary indurated painless  genital ulcer.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:275-277.
